title: Privilege as a response to a pleaded claim
shortTitle: Privilege as a response to a pleaded claim
summary: A privilege can protect conduct or statements that might otherwise support liability. The assigned Garcia opinion distinguishes conditional protection, which may depend on facts such as malice, from absolute protection for particular proceedings.
notes: The privilege rules are substantive and setting-specific. Garcia’s treatment should not be generalized to every employment communication or proceeding.

sections.Meaning: A privilege can protect conduct or statements that might otherwise support liability. The assigned Garcia opinion distinguishes conditional protection, which may depend on facts such as malice, from absolute protection for particular proceedings.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the statement, occasion, legal source of the privilege, and facts relevant to overcoming it. Determine whether the complaint itself establishes the defense or whether factual development remains necessary.
